1.why: All eight screens are static, flat panels with no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays.

2.why: Each step has a large dark-teal heading and a single filled primary button that clearly dominate, though the black 'Logs' panel competes for attention with technical text.

3.why: Each screen presents one task with one or two fields and one button, plus a 'Step X of 6' marker, making the required action easy to locate.

4.why: She must carry over a long random recovery token, a six-digit MFA code, and then type the new password twice on step 4 and again on step 5, plus remember the 12-character composition rules.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager hint, autofill affordance, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: No saved email, masked account hint, or previously used value is displayed anywhere; every field starts empty with nothing to recognize.

7.why: Instructions are one to two short sentences in plain sans-serif at readable size, e.g. 'Enter the recovery token delivered to this secure browser session.'

8.why: No error or validation message is visible in any of the eight screenshots, so the claim cannot be observed to hold.

9.why: Only step 3 shows a concrete value ('Testing code displayed... 482913'); other fields have no placeholder or sample format, and the password rules are stated without an example.

10.why: The flow offers no visible choice of authentication method (no biometric/passkey/alternative code option) — only a fixed password + token + six-digit code sequence.

11.why: Every screen offers exactly one primary action and at most two input fields, so she is never given many options at once.

12.why: The step counter and the final 'Appointment request confirmed' banner communicate progress, but intermediate steps give no explicit success message except cryptic entries in the technical Logs panel.

13.why: Each step includes a short explanatory line, and steps 1 and 4 add an 'Avoid phishing' tip and explicit password composition guidance.

14.why: There is no back link, 'resend code', or 'start over' control on any screen, and step 5 warns verification 'is limited after repeated failures'.

15.why: All screens reuse the identical header, white card, step label, heading style, field styling, primary button and Logs panel layout.
